cohort: This study included 39 pregnant women with influenza during pregnancy (case group) and 39 non-infected pregnant women (control group) from a single center.
finding: Pregnant women infected with influenza had significantly higher rates of cesarean section, neonatal distress, and neonatal hospitalization compared to non-infected mothers.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in pregnant women infected with influenza (63.2%) compared to healthy women (43.5%).
